name: Tokyo
note: Huge city. Stay near Shinjuku or Shibuya so the JR Yamanote loop line is on your doorstep.

name: Shinjuku
note: Neon streets, Omoide Yokocho alleys, Golden Gai bars, the Godzilla head in Kabukicho.

name: Shibuya Crossing
name_ja: 渋谷スクランブル交差点
note: The famous scramble crossing outside Shibuya Station.

name: Shibuya Sky
note: Open-air rooftop on Shibuya Scramble Square. Sunset slots sell out, so book ahead.

name: Meiji Jingu
note: Forest shrine next to Harajuku. Calm early in the morning.

name: Takeshita Street
note: Harajuku street fashion, crepes and candy floss.

name: Senso-ji
note: Tokyo's oldest temple, in Asakusa. Quietest before 8am or after dark.

name: Tokyo Skytree
note: 634 m tower, about 20 minutes on foot from Senso-ji.

name: Akihabara
note: Electronics, anime, figures, retro games, maid cafes.

name: Ikebukuro
note: Big anime shops, Sunshine City and Otome Road.

name: Nakano Broadway
note: Old mall packed with anime, manga and collectibles shops.

name: Ueno Park
note: Museums and the zoo, with Ameyoko market next door.

name: Yanaka Ginza
note: Old-Tokyo shopping street with snack stalls.

name: Tsukiji Outer Market
note: Seafood breakfast and street snacks. Best before 11am.

name: teamLab Planets
name_ja: チームラボプラネッツ
note: Walk-through digital art; you wade through water barefoot. Book tickets ahead.

name: Tokyo Tower
note: The classic red-and-white tower.

name: Imperial Palace East Gardens
note: Free gardens on the old Edo Castle grounds.

name: Shinjuku Gyoen
note: Large landscaped garden. Famous for cherry blossoms.

name: Ghibli Museum
name_ja: 三鷹の森ジブリ美術館
note: Timed tickets go on sale the month before and sell out fast.

name: Shimokitazawa
note: Vintage clothes, record shops, small cafes.

name: Odaiba
note: Waterfront with the life-size Gundam and Rainbow Bridge views.

name: Tokyo Disneyland
name_ja: 東京ディズニーランド

name: Kamakura
note: Seaside temple town, about 1 hour from Tokyo.

name: Kamakura Great Buddha
note: Giant bronze Buddha at Kotoku-in.

name: Yokohama
note: Chinatown, Minato Mirai waterfront, Cup Noodles Museum.

name: Nikko Toshogu
note: Lavishly decorated shrine in the mountains, about 2 hours from Tokyo.

name: Hakone
note: Hot-spring town: Lake Ashi, Owakudani, ropeway, Mt Fuji views on clear days.

name: Owakudani
note: Steaming volcanic valley. Try the black eggs.

name: Hakone Shrine
note: Red torii standing in Lake Ashi.

name: Kusatsu Onsen
note: One of Japan's best hot-spring towns, built around the steaming Yubatake.

name: Narita Airport
note: About 1 hour from central Tokyo by Narita Express or Skyliner.

name: Haneda Airport
note: Close to the city: about 30 minutes to central Tokyo.

name: Kawaguchiko
note: Lake at the foot of Mt Fuji.

name: Chureito Pagoda
note: The postcard view: five-storey pagoda with Mt Fuji behind.

name: Mount Fuji
note: Climbing season is roughly July to early September.

name: Nagoya
note: Castle, miso katsu, and the Ghibli Park nearby.

name: Takayama
note: Preserved merchant town in the Japanese Alps.

name: Shirakawa-go
note: UNESCO village of steep thatched-roof farmhouses.

name: Kanazawa
note: Geisha districts, gold leaf, great seafood.

name: Kenroku-en
note: One of Japan's three great gardens.

name: Matsumoto Castle
note: Original black castle from the 1590s.

name: Kamikochi
note: Alpine valley, open roughly mid-April to mid-November.

name: Jigokudani Monkey Park
note: Snow monkeys bathing in hot springs. Best in winter.

name: Tsumago
note: Edo-era post town on the Nakasendo trail.

name: Magome
note: Hike 8 km from here to Tsumago along the old road.

name: Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route
name_ja: 立山黒部アルペンルート
note: Mountain crossing with snow walls in spring.

name: Kyoto
note: Friend's tip: buses are slow and crowded. Use trains (JR, Keihan, Hankyu, subway) and walk.

name: Fushimi Inari Taisha
note: Thousands of red torii up the mountain. Go around 7am.

name: Kiyomizu-dera
note: Wooden stage temple; walk down Sannenzaka and Ninenzaka after.

name: Kinkaku-ji
note: The Golden Pavilion.

name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove
note: Go early, before the tour groups.

name: Tenryu-ji
note: Zen temple and garden right next to the bamboo grove.

name: Gion
note: Geisha district. Hanamikoji street at dusk.

name: Nishiki Market
note: Covered food market, good for lunch grazing.

name: Ginkaku-ji
note: Silver Pavilion and its moss garden.

name: Philosopher's Path
note: Canal-side walk between Ginkaku-ji and Nanzen-ji.

name: Nijo Castle
note: Shogun's palace with squeaking nightingale floors.

name: Sanjusangen-do
note: Hall of 1,001 Kannon statues.

name: Nara
note: Old capital, easy from Kyoto or Osaka.

name: Nara Park
note: Free-roaming bowing deer. Buy shika senbei crackers for them.

name: Todai-ji
note: Huge wooden hall with a 15 m bronze Buddha.

name: Kasuga Taisha
note: Shrine lined with thousands of lanterns.

name: Osaka
note: Food city. Stay around Namba for Dotonbori.

name: Dotonbori
note: Neon canal and street food: takoyaki, okonomiyaki, kushikatsu.

name: Universal Studios Japan
name_ja: ユニバーサル・スタジオ・ジャパン
note: Super Nintendo World needs a timed entry ticket or Express Pass.

name: Shinsekai
note: Retro district under Tsutenkaku tower, famous for kushikatsu.

name: Kuromon Market
note: Seafood and Wagyu skewers.

name: Umeda Sky Building
note: Floating Garden observatory.

name: Kobe
note: Kobe beef and the harbour.

name: Himeji Castle
note: Japan's finest original castle, a short Shinkansen hop from Osaka.

name: Koyasan
note: Sacred mountain. Stay overnight in a temple.

name: Kinosaki Onsen
note: Seven public baths; stroll between them in a yukata.

name: Ise Jingu
note: Japan's most sacred Shinto shrine.

name: Kumano Nachi Taisha
note: Shrine and pagoda beside Japan's tallest waterfall.

name: Hiroshima
note: Try Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki (layered, with noodles).

name: Hiroshima Peace Memorial Park
note: Atomic Bomb Dome and the Peace Memorial Museum. Plan 2 to 3 hours.

name: Miyajima
note: Floating torii of Itsukushima Shrine. Check the tide table.

name: Okayama Korakuen
note: One of Japan's three great gardens.

name: Kurashiki
note: Willow-lined canal old town.

name: Onomichi
note: Start of the Shimanami Kaido cycling route.

name: Izumo Taisha
note: Ancient shrine with a giant straw rope.

name: Naoshima
note: Art island: Chichu Art Museum and Yayoi Kusama's pumpkin.

name: Dogo Onsen
note: Historic bathhouse in Matsuyama.

name: Ritsurin Garden
note: Large strolling garden in Takamatsu.

name: Iya Valley
note: Remote gorge with vine bridges.

name: Fukuoka
note: Hakata ramen and riverside yatai food stalls.

name: Kumamoto
note: Home prefecture of One Piece creator Eiichiro Oda.

name: Kumamoto Castle
note: Huge castle still being restored after the 2016 earthquakes.

name: Mount Aso
note: Active volcano; crater access depends on gas levels.

name: Takachiho Gorge
note: Rowboats under a waterfall in a basalt gorge.

name: Beppu
note: The 'hells': colourful boiling hot springs.

name: Sakurajima
note: Active volcano, a short ferry ride from Kagoshima.

name: Yakushima
note: Ancient cedar forest island.

name: Fukuoka Airport
note: Very close to Hakata Station.

name: Shuri Castle
note: Being rebuilt after the 2019 fire.

name: Okinawa Churaumi Aquarium
note: Whale sharks.

name: Ishigaki
note: Beaches and snorkelling.

name: Sendai
note: Gyutan (grilled beef tongue).

name: Matsushima
note: Bay dotted with pine-covered islets.

name: Ginzan Onsen
note: Wooden ryokan along a river, magical in snow.

name: Kakunodate
note: Samurai district.

name: Sapporo
note: Miso ramen, beer, the Snow Festival in February.

name: Otaru
note: Canal town with glassworks.

name: Hakodate
note: Night view from Mt Hakodate, morning market.

name: Niseko
note: Powder snow skiing.

name: Furano
note: Lavender fields in July.
